title: Salesforce Stock Surges 14% as AI Revenue Triples and Anthropic Investment Delivers $2.6 Billion Gain
excerpt: The cloud software giant beat earnings estimates on every metric, raised full-year guidance, and announced an expanded AI partnership with Anthropic called Claudeforce.
body:
• Salesforce shares surged 14% in extended trading after the company reported second-quarter revenue of $11.35 billion, up 11% year over year, beating Wall Street estimates.
  • Net income climbed 87% to $3.53 billion, boosted by a $2.6 billion gain on the company's investment in AI startup Anthropic, which was recently valued at $965 billion.
  • Annual recurring revenue from Agentforce and Data 360, Salesforce's AI products, more than tripled year over year to nearly $3.9 billion.
  • Salesforce announced an expanded partnership with Anthropic called "Claudeforce" that will integrate Claude AI models across its enterprise platform.

AI Drives an Earnings Beat

Salesforce shares jumped 14% in after-hours trading on Wednesday after the cloud software company posted second-quarter results that exceeded Wall Street forecasts on revenue, profit, and forward guidance — powered by accelerating demand for its artificial intelligence tools.

Revenue for the quarter ended July 31 rose 11% to $11.35 billion, topping analyst estimates of $11.33 billion. The figure included a $456 million contribution from Informatica, which Salesforce acquired in November 2025.

Net income climbed 87% to $3.53 billion, or $4.29 per share, compared with $1.89 billion, or $1.96 per share, a year earlier. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $5.90, nearly doubling the $3.27 consensus estimate. A significant portion of the beat came from a $2.6 billion gain on strategic investments, primarily Salesforce's stake in Anthropic, the AI company that raised funding valuing it at $965 billion in May.

AI Revenue Triples

The standout metric was the growth of Salesforce's AI business. Annual recurring revenue from Agentforce and Data 360 — the company's agentic AI products — reached nearly $3.9 billion, more than tripling year over year.

"AI is delivering value across every layer of our platform. We're seeing incredible demand for our AI and data products, with ARR about to cross $4 billion."

— Marc Benioff, CEO, Salesforce

The company has delivered over 7 billion "agentic work units" — a metric Salesforce uses to measure work completed by AI — across Agentforce and Slack, with 3.2 billion in the second quarter alone. Chief Financial and Chief Operating Officer Robin Washington told MarketWatch that higher usage of agentic work units is complementing, not replacing, core seat growth.

Current remaining performance obligations, the value of signed contracts expected to convert into revenue within 12 months, reached $33.5 billion, marking 14% year-over-year growth and exceeding estimates. After two quarters of 13% growth, the acceleration was one of the report's biggest highlights, according to Jefferies analyst Jeffrey Favuzza.

Anthropic Partnership Deepens

Alongside earnings, Salesforce announced an expanded strategic partnership with Anthropic called "Claudeforce." The initiative will integrate Anthropic's Claude AI models directly across Salesforce's workplace applications, building on their June collaboration that added an AI agent to Slack.

Salesforce has been an investor in Anthropic since the AI company's Series C funding round in 2023. Other major technology companies, including Alphabet and Microsoft, have similarly reported gains from their Anthropic investments in recent weeks.

Stripping out the investment gain, Salesforce's adjusted earnings would have been $3.37 per share — still above estimates.

Raised Guidance

Salesforce bumped its full-year revenue forecast to between $46.1 billion and $46.4 billion, up from a prior range of $45.9 billion to $46.2 billion. The company raised its annual adjusted earnings per share forecast to $16.67 to $16.71, reflecting both organic growth momentum and a reduction in share count.

For the fiscal third quarter, Salesforce guided for revenue between $11.42 billion and $11.50 billion, positioning slightly above consensus expectations. The guidance implies continued 14% growth in current remaining performance obligations.

The updated full-year outlook also factors in expected contributions from pending acquisitions of Contentful and Fin, which Salesforce expects to close in the coming weeks.

What's Next

At market close on Wednesday, Salesforce stock was down 22% year to date, weighed by concerns that AI tools were eroding demand for traditional enterprise software. The after-hours jump — the largest post-earnings move since August 2024 — suggests investors are warming to evidence that Salesforce's AI investments are translating into revenue growth rather than just hype.

The stock has risen 33% from its recent low at the end of July, as investors have started reconsidering the bearish AI thesis that gripped enterprise software names earlier in the year. Whether the momentum holds will depend on whether Agentforce's rapid revenue growth converts into sustained organic acceleration.
